The main takeaway from our work is that
the copper-ligand bonds in proteins are generally much shorter than those observed in complexes of copper with small molecules, and that this is especially true for Cu-O bonds.

the copper-ligand bonds in the different types of copper site in proteins can be reliably predicted based on their structural and electronic properties, which is of importance to understand the role of the copper ion in the different biological processes in which it participates.
